attacks.claim: Partner-chosen filenames (via src.stem and local path) are interpolated unquoted into a shell=True command string. A crafted filename can inject arbitrary commands on workers holding GCS write credentials for the whole raw bucket.

partition_date() switched from UTC to naive local time. Workers run with TZ=America/Los_Angeles and the job runs at 01:30 UTC, so the dt partition is the previous day. This misaligns with the UTC-date partition dashboards read and can collide with the prior day's data.

Per-file failures are swallowed, yet the _SUCCESS marker is written unconditionally. Dashboards read the partition as soon as the marker appears, so a partition missing files, or holding partial chunks, is published as complete. The task also exits successfully with only a log line, so alerting will not notice.
attacks.evidence:
except Exception:
            log.exception("partner=%s file=%s failed", partner, src.name)
            failed += 1
    write_success_marker(BUCKET, f"raw/{partner}/dt={dt}/")

attacks.claim: A file that fails mid-upload leaves already-uploaded chunks in the partition with no cleanup or retry. Local chunk files and gzip handles are not cleaned on error because there is no try/finally, and unlink only runs after a successful upload.
Empty or header-only input files produce zero chunks but are counted as ok, so the partner's file is silently dropped with no error.
attacks.evidence: for chunk in _write_chunks(src, work_dir): ... ok += 1  # _write_chunks returns [] when no rows

attacks.claim: Reruns are not idempotent. Index-named chunks under a per-file prefix are never cleared, so a rerun into the same partition can leave stale chunks from a previous larger run mixed with new ones. Untrusted src.stem also flows unvalidated into the object path.
attacks.evidence: dest = f"gs://{BUCKET}/raw/{partner}/dt={dt}/{src_name}/{local.name}"  # no clearing of prior prefix

attacks.claim: The output layout changed from one object per file to a directory of numbered chunks, and ingest_partner gained a required work_dir argument. The diff shows no caller or downstream reader updates, so existing callers and consumers may break.
attacks.evidence: def ingest_partner(partner: str, drop_dir: Path, work_dir: Path) -> None: ... dest = f"gs://{BUCKET}/raw/{partner}/dt={dt}/{src_name}/{local.name}"

attacks.claim: The gsutil subprocess has no timeout or retry, so a hung transfer blocks the nightly run and one transient failure permanently fails the file for the night.
attacks.evidence: subprocess.run(... shell=True, check=True)  # no timeout, no retry

attacks.claim: normalise_row now receives a csv.DictReader dict rather than a pandas Series, and the writer header is fixed from each chunk's first normalised row. The claim that normalisation is unchanged is unverified, and no tests were added.
